raw_comment:
1. The graph shows the drought concentration throughout the United States, based on the last week of October in 2024. I noticed that more landlocked states like Kansas, Missouri, and Oklahoma have a more intense drought in their counties. While states that have a portion of its land touching water like California, Florida, and Georgia don’t have as severe of a drought in their counties. 
2. One thing when looking at this graph that caught me off guard was the lack of severity in droughts that California has. I have family that lives in California and it feels like every day I hear their concerns about their water supply becoming more and more limited because of the droughts. California does not tend to receive as many storms as Florida does and also receives a lot of wildfires, which makes me wonder why California’s drought severity is so low. 
3. This relates to my community because it gives me a better sense of understanding of how certain states in the United States need better/more programs to receive clean and drinkable water. While us Floridians don’t usually think about this problem since we are blessed with frequent storms, easy location to the ocean, and Lake Okeechobee, it also relates to my family’s awareness of the drought situation in other parts of the United States. 
4. Headline: Damaging droughts scatter the U.S., is your state next?
